title: Extinct forms fill gaps between existing genera, families and orders

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Extinct forms fill gaps between existing genera, families and orders

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: All fossils can be classed in existing groups or between them, and extinct forms fill up the wide intervals between existing genera, families and orders, forming with living forms one natural system.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. X: On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: That the extinct forms of life help to fill up the wide intervals between existing genera, families, and orders, cannot be disputed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter X, “On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings”; section “On the affinities of extinct species to each other and to living species”. Scope: all extinct and living organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch10-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.60

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Selected clades permit explicit disparity and phylogenetic tests. The universal and classification-dependent wording prevents full resolution with a single non-circular analysis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Add fossil taxa to morphological phylogenetic matrices and measure whether disparity gaps and branch lengths among extant higher groups shrink. Refutation would be widespread fossils falling outside existing-group relationships or failing to reduce the specified gaps.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Fill gaps' lacks a unique quantitative definition.

Higher-group classification is partly constructed from the same characters being tested.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.42
data existence: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.63
data adequacy: 0.51
analysis feasibility: 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Gap-filling is measurable as a reduction in morphological distance once fossils are added, and public matrices exist for many vertebrate and invertebrate clades. They do not cover all organisms, and the placement of fossils is not fully independent of the gaps. The analysis is realistic for several major groups and not for the universal scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In character matrices, measure morphological distances among living orders and families with fossils excluded and again with fossils included. Fossils that sit in the gaps and shrink those distances would support the claim; fossils that only repeat living clusters would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matrices cover some clades well and most of life poorly.

The characters that define the gaps are also the characters used to place the fossils.

Harmonizing many matrices into one analysis takes months.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.45
data existence: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.5
